# 元始天尊說梓童帝君應驗經

**ID:** KR5a0028
**Custom ID:** ZB5a0028

**Editions:** SJB, ZHDZ

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A four-folio Daoist cult-scripture for the Zǐtóng-Wénchāng cult, framed as an audience at the heavenly court of Yuánshǐ tiānzūn 元始天尊. The Divine Lord of Zǐtóng (Zǐtóng dìjūn 梓潼帝君, conventionally Wénchāng 文昌) vows to save all living creatures from the impending *jié* 劫 ("kalpa") disasters. The scripture enumerates the Lord's "responses and proofs" — instances of divine intervention that demonstrate his salvational efficacy — and closes with his divine appellation (*hàohào* 號號). The text is the shorter and more compact of the two Daozang Zǐtóng cult scriptures (with *[DZ 29 Zǐtóng dìjūn běnyuàn jīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0029)*, 12 folios).

**Abstract**

The scripture dates from after 1194, as established by its reference to the "ninety-four transformations" (九十四化) of the Zǐtóng dìjūn (3b) — the transformation-count fixed by the ninety-four-chapter recension of the hagiography *[DZ 170 Zǐtóng dìjūn huàshū 梓潼帝君化書](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0170)* whose last fourteen episodes were completed in 1194. Terry Kleeman, in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 2:1206–1207 (§3.B.11, "The Wenchang Cult"), dates the scripture to the period 1191–1267, though allowing that the ninety-four-chapter recension remained in circulation into the Yuán.

Notably, the scripture identifies the Zǐtóng dìjūn not with the traditional cult-centre at Qīqū shān 七曲山 (in Zǐtóngxiàn 梓潼縣, northern Sichuan) but with the alternative cult-site at Fènghuáng shān 鳳凰山 — suggesting that the text derives from a rival cult-centre in the Zǐtóng area in the closing Southern Sòng. The frontmatter brackets composition notBefore 1194 / notAfter 1279 (close of Southern Sòng), with dynasty 南宋. The deity is wikilinked in frontmatter under [文昌帝君](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%87%E6%98%8C%E5%B8%9D%E5%90%9B) — his canonical Daoist identity — with *(attributed)* marking the revealed-scripture convention.
